text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police find half kg (one lb) of unusually pure heroin and arrest Libyan national during raid on apartment in St Paul's Bay, 10 miles (16 km) north of Valletta.
- Opposition Nominees Act to be repealed; law enacted by former Nationalist government in 1995 allowed opposition to nominate representative on various government boards.
- Maltese workers in Albania staying on despite troubles; workers are involved in charities and an oil services company.

- Government expected to announce decision to extend hospital whose construction began under previous government last year; it will be Malta's main general hospital; existing 60-year-old hospital nearby will then be closed.
- Prices of a number of products rise despite ruling Labour Party promise to control cost of living.
- Woman found dead at sea identified as Irish national Margaret Mary Stanlan, who was in Malta on holiday.
- Strong seas and rough winds prevent 14 ships from entering Grand Harbour.
